name: DPN AI Long-Term Memory & Persistent Knowledge Graph v6
description: Project-scoped durable memory, semantic recall, decision history, provenance-aware knowledge graphs, contradiction handling, stale-fact refresh, and controlled forgetting.
instructions: Use plan_persistent_memory for non-trivial memory-heavy or cross-session project work.
Treat recalled memory as evidence with confidence and provenance, never as unquestioned ground truth.
Prefer project-scoped memory over global memory when the active project is known.
Record explicit decisions, durable constraints, verified facts, artifact lineage, repository relationships, and repeatable procedures when they are likely to matter later.
Do not promote guesses or model inferences to durable fact without supporting evidence.
For time-sensitive facts, refresh against current authoritative evidence before relying on memory.
When two memories conflict, preserve both, compare provenance and dates, mark contradiction or supersession, and avoid silent overwrite.
Distinguish historical truth from current truth. A superseded decision may remain valuable history but must not be treated as active policy.
Use score_memory_candidate when deciding whether new information should stay ephemeral, become project memory, become durable memory, or be quarantined for review.
Preserve source identity, timestamps, project scope, confidence, artifact/file references, and graph relationships when storing important memory.
Repository and artifact memory should link projects, repos, branches, files, components, issues, PRs, decisions, generated artifacts, tests, and releases when evidence supports those relationships.
Never store plaintext secrets, credentials, access tokens, API keys, passwords, or private key material in ordinary memory.
Controlled forgetting must have an explicit scope and reason. Prefer superseding or demoting stale information over destructive deletion when historical provenance remains useful.
Bound recall so large memory stores do not swamp the active task; rank by relevance, project match, provenance, recency, confidence, and contradiction state.
When memory materially changes an answer or action, disclose which remembered decision/fact influenced the result and any uncertainty that remains.
